messages.subject: returning multiple objects
parts:
Hi all,

I bet this one's easy.  In my app, I use source() in server.R to call my main script.  In that script I create a number of objects / df's.  What's the best way to return those objects to make them usable by other reactive functions.  This is what I do now, but it seems clumsy:

run_main_script = reactive( {
blah
source(filename)
 
data_frames = list(raw_data, summary_v1, model_output)   
return(data_frames)
})

Then to refer to those dataframes:

  output$temp = renderTable( {
    t1 = raw_data()[[1]]
    function(t1)
    t1
  })

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: returning multiple objects
parts:
That's a fine way to do it (see below for caveat), though I'd make it a named list and also pass local=TRUE to source:

main = reactive( {
blah
source(filename, local=TRUE)
 
data_frames = list(raw_data=raw_data, summary_v1=summary_v1, model_output=model_output)

})

Then to refer to those dataframes:

output$temp = renderTable( {
    t1 = main()$raw_data
    function(t1)
    t1
  })

Now, it only makes sense to source your file inside a reactive if your calculations actually depend on other reactives (input$xxx, for example). If not, you may as well just do the calculation outside of a reactive and directly reference those calculated variables in the render functions. Render functions can read non-reactive values just fine; they (the non-reactive values) just won't trigger the render function to re-execute, that's all.
